source_scope: Official AOSP Android15 tag android-15.0.0_r1, plus Android35 SDK source view; not exact emulator image fingerprint or every OEM implementation
conclusion: In inspected AOSP implementation, a nonempty fixed-length streamed POST body is not transparently replayed after complete write and lost HTTP response. A later application retry must reserve the batch again.
minimal_required_controls: Keep setFixedLengthStreamingMode(bytes.length) before getOutputStream/connect. A Content-Length header alone is insufficient.
Persistently reserve batch.length event-transmission slots before getOutputStream, conservatively consuming slots even if body transmission fails.
Do not reset spent/reserved slots on revoke, restart or ACK loss; every explicit retry reserves again.
limits: Connection/TLS/route attempts may retry before a body sink exists; these do not retransmit event bodies.
This budgets logical HTTP event submissions, not TCP packet retransmissions, DNS/TLS operations, or downstream server/proxy processing.
ACK loss remains ambiguous: the server may have accepted the first attempt; explicit retries may produce duplicates and must count again.
No undocumented retry property, hidden-platform API, reflection or new dependency is proposed.
No PostHog request, Android execution or TLS ACK-loss experiment was performed by this review.

source_lines.435-436: A follow-up requiring the same non-RetryableSink body throws HttpRetryException.
source_lines.494-505: IOException recovery delegates to HttpEngine.recover; otherwise exception propagates.
source_lines.628-637: Both public fixed-length overloads set the same length used by newHttpEngine.

source_lines.231-251: Buffered mode creates RetryableSink; streaming mode creates a transport sink.
source_lines.367-384: IOException recovery requires StreamAllocation.recover to accept the body; one-argument overload passes the original requestBodyOut.
source_lines.596-609: Response reading closes the written body; only RetryableSink gets body replay before response reading.

source_lines.333-350: IOException recovery is rejected unless requestBodyOut is null or RetryableSink.
source_lines.355-363: Protocol and interrupted I/O errors are not recovered.

source_lines.29-39: HTTPS delegates to the same HttpURLConnectionImpl implementation.

source_lines.285-286: The int fixed-length overload used by DirectQueue forwards to its delegate.

source_lines.122-123: Streaming HTTP/2 body uses stream.getSink rather than RetryableSink.

hash_note: SHA256 is provided only for decoded source bytes whose digest was actually recorded; null means no digest recorded, not a content mismatch.
